claude_proposed_widenings.name: Attachment.object
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Tree Form changes the staff itself into another form. The current activation surface can only attach direct effects to self, target, area, or mark, so the existing alter_item_kind atom cannot be aimed at the staff as an object.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "You can take a Magic action to plant one end of the staff in earth in an unoccupied space and expend 1 charge to transform the staff into a healthy tree."

claude_proposed_widenings.name: ItemDestructionPolicy.last_charge_roll_nonmagical
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The last-charge failure does not destroy the item; it strips its magic and leaves behind an ordinary Quarterstaff. Existing destruction policies only cover destruction or permanent exhaustion.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "If you expend the last charge, roll 1d20. On a 1, the staff loses its properties and becomes a nonmagical Quarterstaff."

claude_proposed_widenings.name: EffectAtom.fall_on_end
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Reverting from tree form causes creatures in the tree to fall. That is a deterministic mechanical rider, but the current surface does not include the taxonomy's fall-on-end effect atom.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "Any creature in the tree falls when the tree reverts to a staff."
